title: Submission approve/reject has no authorization: any self-issued API key can review any submission
description:
SubmissionService.Review never receives the caller's identity. There is no actor parameter at all, and the emitted event hardcodes the actor:

  backend/app/smart_contract/services/submission_service.go:169  func (s *SubmissionService) Review(ctx, submissionID string, body SubmissionReviewInput)
  backend/app/smart_contract/services/submission_service.go:191  s.store.UpdateSubmissionStatus(...)  // no ownership check
  backend/app/smart_contract/services/submission_service.go:201  Actor: "reviewer"  // hardcoded

The REST route only wraps the handler in an API-key check, never an ownership check. The MCP surface has the identical gap in handleApproveSubmission / handleRejectSubmission (backend/mcp/http_mcp_server.go:1099).

Because API keys are self-serve, any anonymous caller can approve or reject any submission on the node. Approval gates payout and rework resolution, so this is the highest-impact finding in the review.

This is structural, not a missing guard clause: the reviewer identity is not plumbed into this layer, so the fix changes the service signature and both call sites (REST + MCP).

Discovered during a full-repo code review on 2026-09-13 (build clean, `go test ./...` green across all 25 packages).
acceptance_criteria: Review() takes an authenticated actor and rejects callers who are not the wish creator or an authorized reviewer. REST and MCP share one enforcement path. Emitted events record the real actor. Regression tests cover wrong-actor reject for both surfaces.
notes:
Triaged in #stargate chat 2026-09-13 with maya (independent code read, claims re-verified locally). Confirmed independently by maya. Two implementation details found during triage that should shape the fix:
(1) There is already a working pattern in-repo to copy rather than invent: requireAuthorizedApprover (mcp/http_mcp_server.go:1167), which the proposal approval path calls at :1061. The submission handlers should use the same helper.
(2) The MCP handlers already RECEIVE the caller identity and discard it -- handleRejectSubmission (:1099) and handleApproveSubmission (:1135) both take an apiKey parameter that is never referenced in the body. So on the MCP side this is a smaller fix than 'plumb identity through': the identity is in scope, just unused. The REST path (handleSubmissionReview -> SubmissionService.Review) is where the signature change is actually needed.
Room consensus: ship this first, together with irl.7.
IN PROGRESS 2026-09-13. Implemented by consolidating rather than patching twice, since enforceCreatorApproval (REST) and requireAuthorizedApprover (MCP) turned out to be ~55 lines of duplicated logic including the same irl.2 fail-open.

New app/smart_contract/authz.go:
  WishCreatorAuthorizer{Keys, Ingestion}.Authorize(apiKey, visibleHash, subject) - the single rule
  ProposalWishHash(proposal) / SubmissionWishHash(store, submission) - hash resolution
  Server.AuthorizeSubmissionReview(ctx, apiKey, submissionID) - exported so MCP shares it

Submission carries no wish reference, so resolution walks submission -> task -> contract and strips the 'wish-' prefix. Fails CLOSED when that chain breaks (no task, no contract), which is a new denial rather than a preserved fail-open - the irl.2 allowance only covers 'wish exists but has no creator_wallet'.

Call sites now: enforceCreatorApproval and requireAuthorizedApprover both delegate (each is a one-liner); handleSubmissionReview returns 403; handleApproveSubmission and handleRejectSubmission use the apiKey they were already discarding.

Side effect: irl.2's fail-open is now ONE branch in authz.go instead of two, so that bead is now a few-line change.

8 new tests in app/smart_contract/authz_test.go cover stranger denied, creator allowed, unbound key denied, unresolvable submission denied, missing submission denied, prefix stripping, wallet-binding requirement, global auditor. Full suite green, no regressions. NOT yet committed.
REVIEW 2026-09-13 by Sol in #stargate: current diff is NOT complete, do not commit. All blockers verified locally:

1. CONFIRMED (P0). Authorize still fails open when creator_wallet is unavailable (authz.go:40-52), so submission approve/reject is still bypassable for wishes with no recorded creator. Critically, the stego reconcile path never writes creator_wallet (stego_reconcile.go:420-438 sets stego_image_cid, visible_pixel_hash, etc. but not creator_wallet), so EVERY peer-replicated / chain-reconciled contract lands in the fail-open branch. Only locally created wishes get it (inscription_handler.go:584,672). Sol's refinement is better than treating this as all-or-nothing: submission review must fail CLOSED now, while proposal approval may keep the compatibility allowance as an explicit separate policy until irl.2.

2. CONFIRMED. Reviewer identity is still not propagated. Review() has no actor param (submission_service.go:169) and still emits Actor: "reviewer" (:201). This bead's own acceptance criteria require the real actor to be recorded, so the criteria are not met.

3. CONFIRMED. MCP approve/reject authorize correctly but then call h.store.UpdateSubmissionStatus directly (http_mcp_server.go:1127, :1164), bypassing SubmissionService.Review and therefore skipping maybeResolveRework (:198) and event emission (:200). REST and MCP diverge on side effects, not just on authorization. Overlaps bead fhz.

4. CONFIRMED. Tests exercise AuthorizeSubmissionReview directly, so they prove the rule but NOT that the handlers call it. Need wrong-actor rejection through the REST route and the MCP tool, plus missing-creator denial for submission review.

5. PARTIALLY WRONG. http_mcp_server.go does have a gofmt diff, but it is pre-existing, not from this change: the only hunk is map-literal alignment in handleCreateProposal (~:1021) and the file already failed gofmt at HEAD. Fixing it is fine but is unrelated churn.

Sol confirmed hash resolution and the stranger/unknown-key denials are sound.
TRIAGE of Sol's review by maya (#stargate, 2026-09-13) - supersedes the blocker classification above:

BLOCKING (agreed by both): Sol #1 fail-open must not apply to submission review ('that is a payout gate'), and Sol #3 MCP must route through SubmissionService.Review rather than calling UpdateSubmissionStatus directly. Proposal approval MAY keep the irl.2 compatibility branch, but as an explicit policy rather than a shared default - so Authorize needs to distinguish its two callers instead of applying one rule to both.

NOT BLOCKING: Sol #2 (actor propagation) is downgraded by maya to a cheap follow-up - 'Authz closes the hole. Actor:"reviewer" is an audit gap. Fix it if the wallet is already in hand at Review; don't hold the commit for a string.' Since Authorize already resolves the bound wallet, threading it through is close to free, but it must not gate the commit. This overrides the 'acceptance criteria not met' framing in the note above: the audit-trail criterion moves to follow-up.

STILL REQUIRED: Sol #4 surface-level tests. maya's rationale is worth keeping - 'helper-only tests would have missed the MCP bypass', which is exactly what happened. Need wrong-actor denial through the REST route AND the MCP tool, plus missing-creator denial on submission review.

Agreed work list: fail closed on submissions, route MCP through Review, add both surface tests, gofmt.

PROCESS BLOCKER: maya cannot see authz.go - Sol reviewed a local diff and maya's tree is still at the pre-export state. She asked that the patch be pushed somewhere readable before commit. Eric has elected to keep this work on dev rather than a feature branch, and to control commits/pushes himself, so this is pending his decision, not an oversight.
close_reason: All four acceptance criteria verified against dev at 2ff6ac2, not assumed. (1) Review takes an authenticated actor: submission_service.go:195 signature includes ReviewActor. (2) REST and MCP share one enforcement path: SubmissionReviewGate built at authz.go:213 and http_mcp_server.go:248, and the MCP-side duplicate was deleted. (3) Events record the real actor: submission_service.go:239 emits the wallet the gate authorized. (4) Wrong-actor regression tests on both surfaces: TestRESTSubmissionReviewRejectsStranger and TestMCPApproveSubmissionRejectsStranger / TestMCPRejectSubmissionRejectsStranger, all passing. Landed across #1 (gate), #3 (ugs: enforcement inside the service plus real actor). Full suite green on dev, plain and -race, 21 packages each.

title: Harden authorization and network surface before exposing a node to untrusted networks
description:
Umbrella for findings from the 2026-09-13 review. The recurring theme is that *authentication* is permissionless by design (anyone can mint an API key via POST /api/auth/challenge + /api/auth/verify by signing with a self-generated Bitcoin key -- handlers/auth_handler.go:145,198) while *authorization* is largely absent, and several code paths deliberately fail open when a secret env var is unset.

Consequence: 'requires a valid API key' is currently equivalent to 'anonymous', so every route that checks only key validity is effectively unauthenticated. Children cover the specific gaps plus two non-auth hardening items on the same exposed surface.

Discovered during a full-repo code review on 2026-09-13 (build clean, `go test ./...` green across all 25 packages).
acceptance_criteria: All child issues closed. A node bound to a public interface has no unauthenticated mutating endpoint and no endpoint whose authorization reduces to 'holds any self-issued API key'.
notes:

  2. irl.2 -- fail closed, same PR as the above
  3. irl.4 (pprof + /metrics) and irl.6 (tarball caps, incl. the :916 prefix check) -- cheap wins, do today
  4. irl.3 -- callback HMAC first, ingest-hash follow-up
Deferred: irl.5 standalone (P3, its extraction instance rides along with irl.6). Out of epic scope: a49 before the next storage change, x63 background.

title: ProposalService.Approve trusts a creatorOK bool from its caller; four events still record fictional actors
description:
Follow-up to stargate-irl.7, agreed with maya in #stargate. Not an open exploit
today: REST is the only caller and it does authorize first. It is a structural
hole of the same kind irl.1/ugs closed for submission review.

1. Approve trusts its caller. proposal_service.go:150 is
   Approve(ctx, id, apiKey string, creatorOK bool). The only caller,
   server_proposals.go:100, runs enforceCreatorApproval and then passes the
   literal true. So authorization is a boolean argument, and any second caller
   that passes true is authorized by saying so. That is worse than a missing
   check because it reads as if a check happened. ugs removed exactly this shape
   from SubmissionService.Review; Approve kept it.

   Note Approve already receives apiKey, so it has what it needs to authorize
   itself. ProposalEditGate from irl.7 governs the same creator rule and can be
   reused directly rather than adding another authorizer.

2. Four events still name actors that no key corresponds to:
   - proposal_service.go:230 approve -> "approver"
   - proposal_service.go:288 proposal_create -> "creator"
   - proposal_service.go:391 proposal_create -> "creator"
   - submission_service.go:337 rework -> "claimant"

   irl.7 fixed update ("editor") and publish ("approver"); ugs fixed review.
   These four are the remainder. The approve one matters most: approving a
   proposal is money-adjacent and the record cannot say which key did it.

   The two proposal_create actors may be legitimately unresolvable if creation
   has no authenticated wallet in every path. If so, the outcome is to write
   down why rather than to invent an actor; a literal "creator" that is
   sometimes true and sometimes false is worse than an explicit unknown.

Sequencing: 1 and 2 are one change for approve, since the wallet needed for the
event is what the internal authorization returns. Do not split them.
acceptance_criteria: Approve authorizes internally through ProposalEditGate (or equivalent) instead of accepting creatorOK, and the parameter is deleted so no caller can assert its own authorization. The approve event records the wallet the authorizer accepted. The three remaining fictional actors are replaced with the identity that was actually authorized, or the reason they cannot be is written down. Wrong-actor test calls Approve directly, with no handler, and a mutation removing the internal check fails it.

title: Enforce submission review authorization inside SubmissionService.Review and record the real actor
description:
Follow-up to stargate-irl.1, raised by Sol and confirmed by maya on PR #1. Both
items were deferred deliberately during that PR, not missed. Neither is an open
exploit on the two surfaces that exist today; both are real remaining holes.

1. Authorization lives in the callers, not the service.

   REST handleSubmissionReview (server_proposals.go) and the MCP
   approve/reject handlers (http_mcp_server.go) each call
   Server.AuthorizeSubmissionReview / authorizeSubmissionReview and then call
   SubmissionService.Review. Review itself takes no authenticated actor and
   enforces nothing, so it is callable without an ownership check. Any third
   caller added later - a new tool, a job, a CLI path - gets no protection and
   nothing fails loudly to say so.

   The fix is to push enforcement into Review, so the check cannot be omitted
   by construction rather than by convention. That means Review needs the
   caller identity, which is the same plumbing item 2 needs.

2. Review events hardcode Actor: "reviewer".

   submission_service.go emits smart_contract.Event{..., Actor: "reviewer"}
   regardless of who acted, so the audit trail cannot answer "who approved this
   payout". The authenticated wallet is available at both call sites and is
   discarded.

Doing these together is the point: both need an actor threaded into
SubmissionService.Review, so splitting them means doing that plumbing twice.

Suggested shape (not prescriptive):
  Review(ctx, submissionID, input, actor) where actor carries the authenticated
  wallet; Review authorizes internally via the existing WishCreatorAuthorizer
  and emits Actor: <wallet>. Callers stop pre-authorizing and simply pass who
  they authenticated. Keep the DenyOnMissingCreator / AllowOnMissingCreator
  distinction from irl.1 intact - submissions must stay fail-closed.

Tests worth having, since irl.1 showed helper-level tests miss exactly this
class of gap:
  - Review with no actor, or an actor that does not own the wish, is refused
    even when called directly, not through a handler
  - the emitted event names the authenticated wallet, not "reviewer"
  - the REST and MCP surface tests added in irl.1 still pass unchanged, proving
    the move did not alter behaviour at the surfaces

Context: irl.1 was merged (or is being merged) as an incremental fix with both
of these known-open. Do not treat irl.1's acceptance criteria as met by that
PR; Sol flagged precisely this and maya's call was to keep irl.1 open through
merge and split these out here.
close_reason: Landed on dev via PR #3 (0813360). Authorization moved into SubmissionService.Review with a ReviewActor carrying only the API key; SubmissionReviewGate is built by both REST and MCP; the review event records the wallet the gate authorized instead of the literal "reviewer". A nil authorizer refuses rather than proceeding. Service-level tests call Review with no handler involved, and each guarantee was mutation-checked.

title: create_contract_rework_request accepts any wallet-bound key as the wish creator
description:
Found while implementing irl.1. handleCreateContractReworkRequest (mcp/http_mcp_server.go:1628) correctly requires a wallet-bound API key and rejects a missing one (:1645, :1655), but it never checks that the wallet is the wish creator before recording it:

  requester = keyInfo.Wallet                       (:1650-1653)
  h.store.CreateContractReworkRequest(ctx, contractID, requester, notes)   (:1659)

ContractReworkRequest.Requester is documented in core/smart_contract/types.go:62 as 'wallet address of wish creator', so the field's contract is being violated: any self-issued key can file a rework request against any contract and be recorded as its creator. Same class as irl.1 and irl.7 - a permissionless key performing a workflow-significant write.

Rework requests feed SubmissionService.maybeResolveRework, so this is workflow-affecting rather than cosmetic.

Now cheap to fix: irl.1 introduced WishCreatorAuthorizer in app/smart_contract/authz.go, shared by REST and MCP. This should resolve the contract's wish hash (strip the 'wish-' prefix from contract_id, same as SubmissionWishHash does via task) and call Authorize before creating the request.
acceptance_criteria: handleCreateContractReworkRequest authorizes the caller as the wish creator via WishCreatorAuthorizer before recording the request, and a non-creator wallet is rejected. Test covers the stranger-wallet case.

title: AGENTS.md tells every agent to run `bd sync`, which does not exist in bd 1.2.2 - beads JSONL silently stopped exporting
description:
Root cause of the stale .beads/issues.jsonl, requested by maya in #stargate.

AGENTS.md instructs agents to run `bd sync` in six places, including 'Always run `bd sync` at session end' (:450) and 'Always `bd sync` before ending session' (:478), plus :15, :198, :441, :466-468. That command does not exist in bd 1.2.2:

  $ bd sync
  Error: unknown command "sync" for "bd"

So every agent that followed the documented workflow ran a failing command at session end, believed it had synced, and never exported. AGENTS.md:106 also claims bd 'exports to .beads/issues.jsonl after changes (5s debounce)', which did not happen either.

Observed damage: the committed JSONL was last written Jul 17 and holds 43 records, all closed, all stargate-*. The live Dolt DB on this machine holds 223. A fresh clone or an unhydrated DB therefore shows a project with zero open work.

This is not cosmetic - it already cost a real triage cycle. maya independently reviewed this repo on 2026-09-13, could not see any of the 12 review beads, and reasonably concluded from `bd doctor` plus the 43-closed JSONL that the tree was in fresh-clone state with an empty Dolt backend. title: Consolidate dual wiring: storage.NewAllStores and container.NewContainer build two independent data layers
description:
main() builds a data layer via storage.NewAllStores (backend/stargate_backend.go:284-306), then runHTTPServer builds a second one via container.NewContainer, which re-reads the environment from scratch (backend/container/container.go:46-115). The two are then mixed:

  backend/stargate_backend.go:841  blockMonitor.SetIngestionService(container.IngestionService)
  backend/stargate_backend.go:~845 StartIPFSIngestionSync(ctx, ingestionSvc, ...)   // the *other* service

So the block monitor and the IPFS ingest sync operate through different ingestion handles over the same data, which can disagree if one pool fails and the other succeeds -- exactly the class of bug that is impossible to reproduce. Relatedly allStores.ContractCache is allocated and never used (storage/factory.go:45), because handlers consume container.ContractCache instead.

The NewAllStores factory is the documented intended single source of truth (storage/factory.go:38) and epic stargate-ood phase 7 aimed to land this; the migration is still incomplete. Config sprawl is the supporting symptom: 124 distinct os.Getenv names across ~243 call sites and 50 files, including near-duplicate keys like STARGATE_SYNC_ENABLED vs STARGATE_SYNC_ENABLE.

Discovered during a full-repo code review on 2026-09-13 (build clean, `go test ./...` green across all 25 packages).
acceptance_criteria: One data/ingestion layer is constructed once and injected everywhere. container.NewContainer no longer re-reads storage env vars. Block monitor and IPFS ingest sync share one ingestion service. No unused store is allocated. Duplicate env keys collapsed to one name with a deprecation alias.
notes: Triaged in #stargate chat 2026-09-13 with maya (independent code read, claims re-verified locally). Independently confirmed by maya: NewAllStores and container.Build each spin up their own ingestion service. Room consensus on sequencing: real and worth doing, but schedule it before the next storage-layer change rather than treating it as a security fire. Should not block the irl.* hardening PRs.

title: Stego callback and /api/ingest-hash skip authentication entirely when their secret env var is unset
description:
Two ingestion entry points treat an empty secret as 'no auth required' rather than 'refuse to serve':

  backend/api/data_api_stego.go:51        secret := os.Getenv("STARLIGHT_CALLBACK_SECRET"); if secret != "" { ...verify... }
  backend/handlers/ingestion_handler.go:39  empty STARGATE_INGEST_TOKEN -> authorize() returns true

With STARLIGHT_CALLBACK_SECRET unset, any unauthenticated POST to /api/stego/callback can append inscriptions and set scan results, which are then persisted via StoreBlockData (data_api_stego.go:135-150). Discovered during a full-repo code review on 2026-09-13 (build clean, `go test ./...` green across all 25 packages).

title: Extract smart-contract business rules from dialect stores into app/core services
description:
## Problem

Business rules for claims, submissions, proposal lifecycle, and contract status live **inside** three near-duplicate store implementations:

| File | ~LOC | Role |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `storage/smart_contract/sqlite_store.go` | 1.9k | durable SQLite |
| `storage/smart_contract/pg_store.go` | 2.3k | durable Postgres |
| `storage/smart_contract/memory_store.go` | 1.5k | tests / memory mode |

**~5.7k total**, much of it triplicated policy (status machines, idempotency, supersede rules), not dialect SQL.

That causes silent dialect drift (e.g. claim re-claim, approve conflict checks, “never demote confirmed wish”) and blocks `stargate-jh0` (GORM MCP CRUD): wrapping fat stores in GORM does not remove the second/third policy copy.

## Already extracted (do not redo)

Partial app/service work already exists — extend it, don’t parallel it:

- `app/smart_contract/services/ProposalService` — HTTP-facing create/list/approve orchestration; still calls fat `store.ApproveProposal` / `PublishProposal`
- `app/smart_contract/services/SubmissionService` — review/rework orchestration; still calls fat `store.UpdateSubmissionStatus`
- `app/smart_contract/services/TaskService` — commitment proof helpers only
- Shared pure helpers already in `storage/smart_contract/` (move or re-export from app/core as needed):
  - `PrepareProposalForCreate`, `ValidateProposalForApproval`, `NormalizeContractID`, `populateProposalTasks`, `BuildTasksFromMarkdown`, contract protection / supersede SQL fragments

## Target architecture

```
REST / MCP / sync
        │
        ▼
app/smart_contract/services/*   ← pure policy + orchestration (ONE place)
        │  uses thin Store CRUD + optional Tx
        ▼
storage/smart_contract.Store    ← row load/save, filters, transactions only
   Memory | SQLite | PG | (later GORM stargate-jh0)
```

**Rule of thumb:** if a function decides “is this transition allowed?” or “what side effects run?”, it belongs in `app/` (or pure package under `core/smart_contract`). If it only maps structs ↔ rows, it stays in storage.

## In-scope methods (high-churn, triplicated)

Extract in this priority order (each PR should keep all three dialects green):

### Wave 1 — claims & submissions (MCP hot path)
1. **`ClaimTask`** — status gate (`available`/`claimed`), active-claim conflict, same-wallet idempotency, claim TTL, `contractor_wallet` into merkle_proof, task row updates  
2. **`SubmitWork`** — claim active/submitted, expiry, submission row + claim/task status  
3. **`UpdateSubmissionStatus`** — approve/reject cascades (task + claim reset/complete)

### Wave 2 — proposal lifecycle
4. **`CreateProposal`** — use `PrepareProposalForCreate`; supersede wish contract only when eligible (confirmed/completed protected)  
5. **`ApproveProposal`** — pending-only, validation, sibling reject, dual-approve conflict on contract_id / visible_pixel_hash, supersede wish  
6. **`PublishProposal`** — approved→published; bulk task/claim status transitions

### Wave 3 — contract / wish integrity
7. **`ConfirmContract`** — confirmation fields, status  
8. **`DeleteWish` / rework request create-resolve** — status guards aligned with contract protection  
9. **`UpdateContractStatus` / `UpsertContractWithTasks`** — demotion rules vs confirmed wishes (see recent integrity hardening)

## Out of scope (this issue)

- Introducing GORM for MCP tables (`stargate-jh0` depends on this finishing first)
- Rewriting MCP tool handlers / REST surface for its own sake (they should call the new services; keep URLs/JSON stable)
- Ingestion / IPFS / stego reconcile policy (already mostly in `app/`; only touch if they bypass the new services with raw store status hacks)
- Full merge of Memory into sqlite `:memory:` (optional later)

## Dependencies

- **Discovered-from:** `stargate-e4z` (GORM foundation for keys/blocks — done)
- **Blocks:** `stargate-jh0` (MCP GORM CRUD) — mark dep when x7y waves land enough for thin repos
- **Related:** contract protection / dual-wish hardening on `dev` (must preserve in extracted rules)

## Suggested PR breakdown

| PR | Deliverable | Exit signal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | `ClaimPolicy` + service; stores become transactional CRUD used by service | sqlite+memory tests for claim idempotency/conflict identical |
| B | `SubmitWork` + `UpdateSubmissionStatus` policy | submission review path only hits service |
| C | Approve/Publish/Create proposal policy; thin `ApproveProposal` store ops | `ProposalService` no longer relies on store-embedded state machine beyond SQL |
| D | Confirm/DeleteWish/protection helpers centralized | one table of allowed status transitions in code |

Estimate: multi-session; ~1–2 weeks focused; do not big-bang all 5.7k LOC.
design:
## Design notes

### Package layout (proposed)

```
backend/core/smart_contract/     # pure types + pure transition helpers (no I/O)
  transitions.go                 # ClaimTaskInput → ClaimDecision, ApproveDecision, etc.
  status.go                      # allowed task/claim/proposal/submission statuses

backend/app/smart_contract/services/
  claim_service.go               # NEW — Claim / SubmitWork
  proposal_service.go            # EXTEND — move store-side approve/publish body here
  submission_service.go          # EXTEND — move cascade logic here
  contract_service.go            # NEW — Confirm / status / wish delete

backend/storage/smart_contract/
  store.go                       # SPLIT or document: “fat” methods thin out over time
  # Prefer adding narrow CRUD methods rather than growing Store forever:
  #   GetTaskForUpdate, InsertClaim, UpdateTaskClaimFields, ...
  # Or keep Store methods as facades that call shared policy + dialect exec
  # during migration (strangler), then delete facade bodies.
```

### Strangler pattern (required)

Do **not** delete `SQLiteStore.ClaimTask` on day one while MCP still type-asserts stores.

1. Extract pure decision function (table-driven tests, no DB).  
2. Implement once in service using existing store read/write methods (may add thin helpers).  
3. Change `SQLiteStore` / `PGStore` / `MemoryStore` methods to either:
   - **Facade:** call shared policy then dialect persist (temporary), or  
   - **Delegate:** `return claimService.Claim(...)` if service is injectable (harder for storage package).  

Prefer **policy package in `core/` or `app/services` + thin store writes** so `storage` does not import `app` (dependency direction: app → storage only).

Correct direction:

```
app/services  →  core transitions (pure)
app/services  →  storage.Store (CRUD)
storage/*     →  core transitions (optional, for facade during migration only)
storage/*  ̸→  app  (forbidden)
```

If store facades need shared rules during migration, put pure functions in `core/smart_contract` or keep them in `storage/smart_contract` helpers (already started with `proposal_prepare.go`) and move upward when app owns the call path.

### Transaction boundaries

Claim/Approve need multi-row atomicity. Options:

1. **Store methods stay transactional** but only run SQL produced after pure decision (service returns a `ClaimPlan{insert claim, update task, ...}`; store applies plan in one tx).  
2. **Store exposes `RunInTx(fn)`** + row-level ops; service owns the fn (cleaner long-term; more API surface).

Recommend **option 1 for Wave 1** (less interface churn), **option 2 for Wave 2+** if plan types get large.

### Status transition tables (document in code)

Codify once (today’s behavior — verify against all three stores before “fixing”):

**Task:** `available` → `claimed` → (`submitted`/`pending_review`) → `approved` | back to `available` on reject  
**Claim:** `active` → `submitted`/`complete`/`rejected`; same wallet re-claim of active is idempotent  
**Proposal:** `pending` → `approved` → `published`; sibling pendings for same wish/contract → `rejected` on approve  
**Contract/wish:** never supersede/demote `confirmed`/`completed` via proposal create or approval (see `supersedeEligibleStatusSQL` / contract protection)

### Test strategy

- **Pure unit tests** for each transition (table-driven).  
- **One integration suite** run against Memory + SQLite (temp file); PG optional in CI if DSN present.  
- Reuse/expand: `sqlite_store_test.go`, `proposal_*_test.go`, `auth_security_test.go`, contract protection tests.  
- Golden rule: for each extracted method, assert Memory/SQLite/PG produce same error sentinels (`ErrTaskTaken`, `ErrTaskUnavailable`, …) and same resulting row statuses.

### Call-site migration

After services own policy:

| Caller | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `app/smart_contract/server_*.go` | already uses services for some paths — ensure claim/submit go through ClaimService |
| `mcp/*` | call services (or app Server ports), not fat store methods |
| sync (ingestion/ipfs/stego) | keep using `UpsertContractWithTasks` but via ContractService once protection lives there |

### Success metric

- Lines of **behavioral** code in the three stores drop sharply (target: each store method for Wave 1–2 is mostly SQL).  
- Zero intentional behavior differences between dialects for extracted methods (enforced by shared tests).  
- `stargate-jh0` can implement a single GORM repo for rows without re-encoding approve/claim rules.

title: Replica submission approval needs a creator signature over the wish hash
description:
Submissions on a replicated wish are unapprovable on any node but the origin,
because a mirroring node has no way to establish who created the wish. Closing
that needs a verifiable creator identity, not a metadata copy.

Current state (after stargate-irl.1, branch fix/submission-authz):
  submission review uses DenyOnMissingCreator, so replicas are refused
  proposal approval keeps AllowOnMissingCreator until stargate-irl.2
  STARLIGHT_DONATION_ADDRESS (Global Auditor) is the only replica escape hatch

Why the obvious fixes are wrong. Both were proposed and rejected during
irl.1 review, so please read this before reopening either:

1. manifest.Issuer is not the creator. It is STARGATE_STEGO_ISSUER /
   INSTANCE_ID / hostname / "stargate" (stego_publish.go:78-87), a node label
   validated only as non-empty (stego/manifest.go:34); fixtures use "oracle-1"
   and "tester". Using it would let any replicating node approve payouts on
   every wish it mirrors.

2. Do not copy creator_wallet from the stego payload, even fill-if-absent.
   extractStegoMetadata has no allowlist (stego_publish.go:830-848) so the
   field is embedded on publish, but inbound it is attacker-controlled and is
   deliberately excluded from stegoPayloadMetadataAllowlist
   (stego_security.go:19-27). Two consequences:
     - ensureStegoIngestion calls UpdateFromIngest when the row exists
       (stego_reconcile.go:439-441), and that merges incoming-wins on both
       dialects (mergeMetadataSQLite existing[k]=v service.go:572-574;
       postgres metadata || $6 service.go:411). A crafted replica of an
       existing wish would therefore overwrite the real creator_wallet on the
       origin node, making the attacker the recorded owner.
     - Fill-if-absent only narrows this to first-writer-wins, and on a fresh
       peer the attacker can be first.

The on-chain gate does not supply the missing binding. parseOPReturnHashes
reads wish_hash || stego_hash (block_monitor_reconcile.go:265-273) and
reconcileStegoFromLocalFile rejects a hash mismatch
(stego_reconcile.go:174-179), so the chain binds the image BYTES to the
inscription. But contractID comes from manifest.VisiblePixelHash
(stego_reconcile.go:194), and the no-candidate branch materializes a contract
for a wish the node has never seen (block_monitor_reconcile.go:331-356). No
step extracts a funding input address or ties either hash to a wallet.

What would actually close it: a signature over the wish hash by the creator's
key, carried alongside the wish and verified independently of the payload, so
a replica can check authorship without trusting the carrier. That is a
protocol change and needs a decision on where the signature lives and which
key signs.

Also worth resolving as part of the design: whether Global Auditor should
remain a blanket approver, which stargate-irl.2 already flags.

Do not implement by relaxing the fail-closed rule. If replica approval is
urgent before this lands, Global Auditor is the intended path.

Discussed in #stargate; cursor-agent proposed (1), maya proposed (2), both
withdrawn after tracing the inbound path.

title: Add graceful shutdown: BlockMonitor.Stop/IsRunning are unimplemented comment stubs and main ends in select{}
description:
There is no coordinated shutdown for any background subsystem:

  backend/bitcoin/block_monitor.go:327  Stop() and IsRunning() exist as comments with no implementations
  backend/stargate_backend.go:449       go runHTTPServer(...) then select {}
  backend/stargate_backend.go:496,1061  IPFS mirror retry loops use context.Background() forever
  backend/stargate_backend.go:567       agent orchestrator started with context.Background(), comment notes no Stop yet

Everything relies on process kill. For a process that manages a btcd child, holds SQLite handles and runs libp2p, that risks leaving the managed btcd orphaned and the DB mid-write. Note stargate_backend.go:634 already avoids log.Fatal specifically because it skips defers, so the intent is there but incomplete.

Also in scope: the historical block precache goroutine uses time.Sleep(2s/5s) in the production path (stargate_backend.go:867-899) with no cancellation, so it cannot be interrupted during shutdown.

Discovered during a full-repo code review on 2026-09-13 (build clean, `go test ./...` green across all 25 packages).

title: Sandbox tarball extraction has no size or entry-count limit (decompression bomb)
description:
backend/app/smart_contract/stego_reconcile.go:924  data, err := io.ReadAll(tr)

Unbounded read per tar entry, with no cap on total extracted bytes, per-file size, or entry count. This tarball arrives from peers and is referenced by on-chain commitments, so the content is attacker-supplied: a small stego payload can point at a tarball that exhausts memory or fills the disk on every node that reconciles the block.

Credit where due: the same loop handles tar.TypeReg only, so symlink and hardlink attacks are already closed.

Discovered during a full-repo code review on 2026-09-13 (build clean, `go test ./...` green across all 25 packages).
acceptance_criteria: Extraction enforces a max per-entry size, max total extracted bytes, and max entry count via io.LimitReader, aborting and logging when exceeded. Limits are configurable with safe defaults. Test covers an oversized entry and an excessive entry count.
notes: Triaged in #stargate chat 2026-09-13 with maya (independent code read, claims re-verified locally). Confirmed by room, agreed as a cheap win to do today. Scope note: while adding the size and entry-count caps, also fix the HasPrefix-without-separator check at stego_reconcile.go:916 in this same loop (the extraction-path instance of irl.5). maya also confirmed the TypeReg-only handling is already correct, so symlinks need no work here.

title: Path confinement uses HasPrefix without a separator in 4 places instead of security.SanitizePath
description:
The repo already has a correct helper -- security.SanitizePath compares against baseDir+string(filepath.Separator) (backend/security/path_sanitizer.go:53) -- but four call sites hand-roll a weaker check:

  backend/stargate_backend.go:153   /uploads/  handler
  backend/stargate_backend.go:764   /sandbox/  handler
  backend/stargate_backend.go:968   block-image uploads fallback
  backend/app/smart_contract/stego_reconcile.go:916  tar entry output path

Verified reachable: Go's ServeMux 301-redirects a literal '..' segment, but percent-encoded forms ('/uploads/..%2fsibling%2ffile', '/uploads/%2e%2e/...') survive mux cleaning and arrive at the handler with '../' intact in r.URL.Path, and the prefix check passes.

Severity is limited rather than critical: UPLOADS_DIR is defaulted to data/uploads (stargate_backend.go:392), so an escape only reaches sibling directories that share that string prefix, and none exist in the default or Docker layouts. Filing as a real but latent bug -- it is one config change away from mattering and the correct helper is already available.

Note: /api/block-image/{height}/{filename} was investigated and is NOT vulnerable -- strings.Split on the already-decoded r.URL.Path (stargate_backend.go:937) means filename can never contain a separator, encoded or not.

Discovered during a full-repo code review on 2026-09-13 (build clean, `go test ./...` green across all 25 packages).
acceptance_criteria: All four sites route through security.SanitizePath (or an equivalent separator-aware check). Table test covers percent-encoded traversal ('..%2f', '%2e%2e') and the sibling-prefix case (uploads vs uploads-backup).
notes: Triaged in #stargate chat 2026-09-13 with maya (independent code read, claims re-verified locally). DEPRIORITIZED as a standalone project (P2 -> P3) by room consensus, but NOT dropped. maya's point: the fourth instance of this bug is inside the tarball extraction path (stego_reconcile.go:916), which is exactly the code irl.6 already has to touch to add size caps. So fix that one instance as part of irl.6 and leave the three HTTP-serving instances (stargate_backend.go:153, :764, :968) here as lower-priority cleanup. Agreed rationale: no node is publicly exposed yet, and impact is bounded to sibling directories sharing the path prefix.
